text: A river does not hurry, and still it reaches the sea.
One sealed scroll is a stone laid on the path.
The mountain was climbed one breath at a time.
Rest is also a step on the road.
What you tend each day quietly grows.
The brush moves, the ink dries, the scroll remembers.
Begin where the mist is thin.
A small flame, kept, outlasts a large one, wasted.
The path is made of ordinary mornings.
Even the longest journey is walked in the present step.
Be as the pine: rooted, patient, green in the snow.
Steady water wears the hardest stone.
Today's trial is today's teacher.
Sharpen the blade by using it gently, often.
The lotus opens when it is ready, and not before.
Carry less, walk farther.
Calm is a skill, and it is practised.
Every sealed day is a seed in the cultivator's garden.
The sky does not rush the dawn.
Fall seven times in the mist; the eighth step is still yours.
Gather your focus as the cloud gathers rain.
A quiet mind sees the whole mountain.
Do the next small thing, and let the large thing follow.
The bamboo bends in the storm and keeps its height.
Progress is a lantern, not a fire: it lights the next few steps.
Honour the day you have, not the day you imagined.
The tea cools, the work warms; both are good.
Neither the peak nor the valley is the whole journey.
Patience is power that has learned to wait.
Another day sealed, another leaf upon the scroll.
